pages.title: ROTH vs. Traditional
pages.description: Both options grow your retirement savings — they just differ in when you pay taxes.
body: ROTH (post-tax): You pay taxes now on the money you contribute. When you withdraw in retirement, you won't owe taxes on any of the growth — interest, dividends, or investment returns.
Traditional (pre-tax): Your contribution reduces your taxable income today. When you withdraw in retirement, the IRS taxes everything you take out — your contributions and all growth.

Which is better? Experts disagree. Generally, ROTH works well when you're younger or in a lower tax bracket, but it depends on your goals. Consider talking to a financial advisor to find what's right for you.
